Giddalti
gih-DAL-tie
proper noun
Hebrew giddalti, “I have magnified” or “I have made great,” one of the sons of Heman the king’s seer, set among the temple singers.

📖 Biblical Definition

Giddalti was one of the fourteen sons of Heman, the king’s seer in the words of God, given to him by the LORD to lift up the horn (1Ch 25:4). With his brethren he was appointed to the song of the house of the LORD under his father’s hand, with cymbals, psalteries, and harps, for the service of the sanctuary. When the lots were cast for the courses of the singers, the two and twentieth fell to Giddalti, to him, his sons, and his brethren, twelve in number (1Ch 25:29). His name signifies “I have magnified,” and it belongs to that string of names among the latter sons of Heman which, read in their order, make a small psalm of petition and praise, as though God had written a song into the very cradle-names of this house. The dictionary honours that the LORD ordered the praises of His house down to the casting of the lot, that none should usurp another’s place and none be left without his portion. There is grace here for the singing church, that the worship of God is His own to appoint and to apportion. Giddalti stands as a witness that the chief end of the singer is to magnify the LORD, even as his name declares; for they that are appointed to the song of God’s house are called to make Him great in the eyes of His people, and to keep that holy charge in the order He has set.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

One of the sons of Heman the king’s seer, set among the temple singers by lot.

GIDDALTI, one of the fourteen sons of Heman the king’s seer.

📖 Key Scripture

1Ch 25:4 — "Of Heman: the sons of Heman; Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamtiezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth:"

1Ch 25:29 — "The two and twentieth to Giddalti, he, his sons, and his brethren, were twelve:"

Psa 34:3 — "O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together."

Psa 35:27 — "Let them shout for joy, and be glad, that favour my righteous cause: yea, let them say continually, Let the LORD be magnified, which hath pleasure in the prosperity of his servant."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A man of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses to the singer’s calling to magnify the LORD in His house.

expand to see more

Giddalti the singer is a man of the sacred record, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him. The dictionary records him that the reader who meets the name among the sons of Heman may know him for a real man in a real service, set by a real God to lead the praises of His house.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the singer’s chief end is to magnify the LORD, even as Giddalti’s name declares. He who set this son in the two and twentieth course of the song is the same who calls His people still to magnify Him together and exalt His name. The saint appointed to lead worship may remember Giddalti, whose name means “I have magnified,” and keep the holy charge to make the LORD great in the eyes of His people.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “I have magnified,” Giddalti names a son of Heman among the singers.
